studies.label: In-person pilot of the two-player AUT (GPT vs HUM vs CON, within-person)

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 3, Figure 1 caption; Section 3.2 states that each participant completed every partner condition
counts_source.quote: Each participant (N = 62) runs three randomized 4-minute co-creation sessions—once

arms.name: GPT
arms.description: Each participant completes a live co-ideation chat with a GPT-4 partner and then curates the best creative uses. AI turns are restricted to a single-sentence idea, with server-enforced turn-taking; partner identity is disclosed (PDF pp. 2-3, Sections 3.1-3.2). The randomized count is the within-person cohort, not a separate group.

arms.name: HUM
arms.description: Each participant completes a shared co-ideation chat with another participant, using the same interface and matched task instructions, and then curates the best creative uses. Human turn-taking occurs naturally (PDF pp. 2-3, Sections 3.1-3.2). The randomized count is the same within-person cohort.

arms.name: CON (pooled)
arms.description: Each participant completes a non-interactive session with a pre-rated seed set and then curates uses. This arm pools highly creative human, uncreative human, and GPT-4-only seed sets (PDF p. 3, Section 3.2). The other_aid code follows the reconciled form because the schema has no mixed code; some participants receive AI-generated ideas, so this is not an AI-free control.

arms.name: CON gpt_con
arms.description: CON seed sub-arm showing GPT-4-only ideas, without a live partner. Seed-set assignment is between participants and is not stated to be random (PDF p. 3, Section 3.2 and Figure 1; PDF p. 6, Section 4.3).

arms.name: CON high_con
arms.description: CON seed sub-arm showing highly creative human ideas drawn from Stevenson et al. and selected by agreement between independent researchers. Seed-set assignment is not stated to be random (PDF p. 3, Section 3.2 and Figure 1; PDF p. 6, Section 4.3).

arms.name: CON low_con
arms.description: CON seed sub-arm showing uncreative human ideas drawn from Stevenson et al. and selected by agreement between independent researchers. Seed-set assignment is not stated to be random (PDF p. 3, Section 3.2 and Figure 1; PDF p. 6, Section 4.3).

studies.task: Generate unusual uses for a book, fork, or tin can in a four-minute session with the assigned partner or seed set, then curate the best creative uses in a separate survey tab.

ai_tool.name: gpt-4 via OpenAI chat-completions API
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 3, Section 3.1, AI configuration; the model release year is not stated

preregistration.where: No pilot preregistration is reported. PDF p. 4, Section 4, calls the estimates exploratory; PDF p. 7, Section 7, describes the platform as a pre-registerable testbed.

estimates.outcome: Crowd-rated originality of ideas, GPT partner versus human partner
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Originality is how unlikely others would be to generate the idea, rated independently by crowdsourced workers on a five-point Likert scale (PDF p. 4, Section 3.4). The model analyzes individual ratings, with subject, item-within-subject, and rater random intercepts (PDF p. 4, Section 4). The Figure 1 caption says curated ideas are rated; the diagram also mentions ideas generated in chat plus curated, so inclusion of partner contributions in the scored pool remains unresolved.

regression.model: Linear mixed-effects model with fixed effects of partner type, non-interactive seed-set assignment, and their interaction, and random intercepts for subject, item-within-subject, and rater (PDF p. 4, Section 4). The companion TOST result is the maximum credible-effect bound |β| ≤ 0.33 (Section 4.1); its test statistic and p-value are not printed.

estimates.notes: Main frequentist specification of the paired GPT-minus-HUM contrast. The coefficient and confidence interval are on the raw originality scale; no standardization is stated. Subject random effects account for repeated observations of each participant, so se_basis is participant despite the rating-level observations. Whether dependence within HUM dyads is also modeled is not stated. Analysis-specific participant counts and rating counts are absent; the overall pilot count is not substituted. No first-round-only estimate is printed. Full-sample arm means and SDs are absent, and BAS Drive subgroup summaries are not combined. The TOST bound is retained in the model description and its source because it is not a point estimate or standard error. The Bayesian record re-estimates this same comparison; it is not independent evidence.

estimates.notes: Alternative Bayesian analysis of the same paired GPT-minus-HUM contrast as s1_novelty_gpt_vs_hum_paired_lmm. regression.coef records the printed posterior median, not a frequentist estimate; the CI fields hold a Bayesian credible interval, not a sampling confidence interval, and must not be converted into a frequentist SE. test.type other and test.value denote BF₀₁, evidence for the null relative to the alternative, not a t, F, or z statistic. No posterior SD, SE, p-value, or analysis-specific counts are printed. se_basis=participant follows the paper’s description of this as a re-estimation of the model with subject random intercepts; the Bayesian random-effects formula is not separately printed. Its sign and interval differ from the main frequentist estimate without explanation. Retain as an alternative specification of the full-sample randomized comparison under extraction rule 4 and codebook Section 8. Do not pool both specifications as independent observations, or interpret the Bayes factor as a standardized effect.

not_extracted.what: S1-O2: Crowd-rated originality, GPT versus CON (pooled)
not_extracted.reason: No full-sample GPT-versus-CON contrast is printed. PDF p. 5, Section 4.2, reports a BAS Drive interaction, and PDF p. 6, Figure 3, reports subgroup comparisons. Moderation and subgroup results are excluded. CON also combines human-written and AI-generated seeds.

not_extracted.what: BAS Drive subgroup contrasts in originality, including S1-O1 GPT versus HUM and Figure 3 partner comparisons
not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 6, Figure 3, splits participants by BAS Drive. These are subgroup contrasts, not eligible full-sample estimates. The means are not recombined, and their plotted confidence intervals are not read off the figure.
PDF p. 5, Section 4.2, reports this only as a robustness outcome for the BAS Drive interaction. No full-sample AI-arm contrast or arm levels are printed; moderation results are excluded.

not_extracted.what: S1-O3: CON-session originality, CON gpt_con versus CON low_con
not_extracted.reason: Only the within-person session order is stated to be randomized. The between-person seed-set assignment is not stated to be random (PDF p. 3, Section 3.2 and Figure 1; PDF p. 6, Section 4.3). It is also unclear whether the manipulation check rates seed texts or participant-produced ideas (PDF p. 4, Sections 3.4 and 4.1). Not extracted as a randomized human-assistance contrast.

not_extracted.reason: Only the within-person session order is stated to be randomized. The between-person seed-set assignment is not stated to be random (PDF p. 3, Section 3.2 and Figure 1; PDF p. 6, Section 4.3). It is also unclear whether the manipulation check rates seed texts or participant-produced ideas (PDF p. 4, Sections 3.4 and 4.1). Not extracted as a randomized human-assistance contrast.

not_extracted.what: S1-O4: Later originality by first-session CON seed set, including CON gpt_con versus CON high_con and the omnibus seed-set test
not_extracted.reason: The seed-set assignment is not stated to be random. This analysis is restricted to participants whose first session was CON and pools later HUM and GPT sessions (PDF p. 6, Section 4.3). It therefore does not provide a full-sample randomized AI contrast or a separate outcome produced after AI removal.

not_extracted.what: Trait predictors of originality and within-subject originality range, including RMET, BIS/BAS, and random-forest variable importance
not_extracted.reason: PDF pp. 4-5, Sections 3.3 and 4.2 and Figure 2, analyze measured participant traits, their associations, and their interactions. These are not randomized AI-versus-comparator estimates. Within-person variation is not diversity across people.

not_extracted.what: Partner perceptions and originality associations: outsourcing, responsiveness, competence, influence, and effect
not_extracted.reason: Perception items are self-reports, not creativity scored on produced output; their reported associations with originality are non-randomized correlational or moderation analyses (PDF p. 3, Section 3.2; PDF p. 4, Figure 1 text alternative; PDF p. 5, Section 4.2).

not_extracted.what: Utility of Alternate Uses Test ideas
not_extracted.reason: Defined as practical usefulness, but PDF p. 4, Section 3.4, states: "We report originality here; utility results are available on request." No result is printed.

not_extracted.what: Solo Alternate Uses Test before or after the co-creation sessions
not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 3, Section 3.2, describes the solo task as a baseline or practice control. The paper prints no solo-AUT outcome contrast and does not state that assignment to before versus after was randomized.

open_items: The pilot has a printed overall participant count, but exact participant counts in each mixed-model analysis, per-condition analyzed counts, and the total number of ratings analyzed are absent. n_analyzed and contrast counts remain null; no counts are inferred from degrees of freedom or summed from Figure 3 subgroups.

No full-sample arm means, participant-level SDs, or paired-difference SD/correlation are reported. PDF p. 4, Section 3.4 reports rater-intercept variability; that is not an outcome SD and cannot be used as a standardizer.
No first-round-only GPT-versus-HUM contrast is printed; the extracted results use the paper’s paired analysis.

The rated pool is ambiguous: Figure 1 says curated ideas are rated but also labels the pipeline as ideas generated in chat plus curated. It is unclear whether GPT partner contributions are included in the rated GPT pool.
The PDF does not specify how HUM dyads were formed, whether order randomization operated independently for individuals, or whether the model accounts for dependence between the two human partners.

Seed-set assignment is never called random. The manipulation-check comparison may concern supplied seeds rather than participants’ outputs; neither uncertainty is resolved by randomized order of the partner conditions.
The later-session seed analysis pools HUM and GPT output; separate estimates would be needed to identify an unassisted after-AI outcome.
The Bayesian and frequentist GPT-versus-HUM results have different signs and intervals; the paper does not explain the discrepancy or separately specify the full Bayesian random-effects model.

The document gives inconsistent corpus and rater counts: PDF p. 2, Section 1.1 and Figure 1 report 1,928 ideas, while PDF p. 4, Section 3.4 reports 1,923; the Figure 1 text alternative on PDF p. 4 reports 225 raters, while Section 3.4 reports 226. These are not substituted for contrast-specific counts.
Figure 3 shows unequal BAS Drive subgroup counts across partner conditions without an exclusion explanation. The plotted subgroup means and counts are not used to reconstruct full-sample results.
The model release year and a pilot preregistration are not stated. No preregistered primary outcome can be confirmed.

The citation record identifies a later proceedings version, DOI 10.1145/3803784.3816851. Whether its body changes these results is unverified; this extraction uses only the supplied author-manuscript PDF.
Utility results are available only on request (PDF p. 4, Section 3.4). No supplement or appendix is included or referenced in the saved document.
notes: Reconciled on 2026-10-10 against the entire markdown conversion and all eight PDF pages, including references. All pages were text-extracted with pymupdf, all three embedded figures were inspected in memory, and find_tables found no tables; there is no appendix. PDF and printed page numbers agree wherever printed. The two estimate records are alternative analyses of one full-sample GPT-versus-HUM comparison, not separate samples or outcomes. Primary-record choice (primary_override): s1_novelty_gpt_vs_hum_paired_lmm, because Section 4.1 presents the frequentist LMM coefficient as the main estimate and introduces the Bayesian result as a re-estimation; the latter stays as a sensitivity specification. The TOST bound is preserved with the frequentist model rather than counted as another contrast. Agreement audit confirmed with_ai, novelty, human_raters, unit=rating, higher_is=more_creative, outcome_with_ai=true, immediate timing, ai_vs_active, and within_person=paired from Sections 3.2, 3.4, and 4. AI was available in the ideation session that produced the scored uses; subsequent curation in a survey tab is not a separate unassisted creative task. Subject random intercepts support participant-based uncertainty under the codebook, while dependence within human dyads remains unresolved. The study and main-arm randomized counts refer to the same cohort; analyzed people counts and rating-observation counts remain null because they are not printed for these models. No participant counts are inferred from degrees of freedom, summed from subgroups, or substituted with idea or rater counts. Country is inferred from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign institution named on PDF p. 3. The AI role is other because GPT is a constrained turn-taking co-ideation partner. CON pools human and GPT seed sets and is not an AI-free control; seed-set assignment is not established as random. Every screening outcome and contrast is either represented by S1-O1 or individually covered in not_extracted. No eligible outcome or contrast missed by both extractors was found. No separate diversity outcome or qualifying after-AI contrast is reported. The screening form identifies no other paper sharing these participants; reuse of published seed ideas does not establish a shared participant sample. No arm mean, SD, SE, effect, or interval was calculated. Source quotes retain printed signs and precision; numeric JSON values are transcriptions of those values. Only the supplied author manuscript was used; the later proceedings body was not verified.

resolutions.decision: Keep null (B). The paper states randomized within-person session order and prints no randomized-cluster counts. HUM dyad formation and the implementation of order randomization are unspecified, so no cluster count is inferred.

resolutions.decision: Retain the B-only estimate. Section 4.1 reports a Bayesian re-estimation of the eligible full-sample paired GPT-versus-HUM comparison, not a subgroup, moderator, nonrandom study, or model-only arm. Codebook Section 8 allows alternative analysis specifications while selecting one primary record. Keep the frequentist LMM as the primary specification, label the posterior median and credible interval explicitly, and identify the Bayes factor as test.type other. The two records must not be pooled as independent evidence.
